findings.description: The database username and plaintext password are interpolated into EC2 user data and written to a local PHP configuration file. User data can be retrieved by principals or processes able to access instance metadata or launch configuration, exposing database credentials.

The RDS instance is configured with publicly_accessible = true, assigning it a public network address. Although the shown security group restricts inbound MySQL to the VPC CIDR, this unnecessarily exposes the database to an Internet-facing routing surface and can become externally reachable if network controls change.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the database storage and its automated backups unencrypted at rest, exposing stored data if underlying storage or snapshots are accessed improperly.

This rule permits all protocols and ports from the database security group to 0.0.0.0/0. It creates unnecessary outbound attack surface and enables unrestricted exfiltration from a compromised database instance.

The EC2 application role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on every resource. Compromise of the application instance would provide broad control over storage, compute, and databases rather than only the minimum permissions required.
